briefs.source_chain: US strikes on Iranian targets near the Strait of Hormuz (after Iran's weekend missile attack on a US base in Jordan) and Iran's retaliation push Brent +4.60% to $94.65 and EU gas to a 3-yr high, therefore higher energy prices lift inflation/rate expectations and push global bond yields to multi-year highs, therefore equities sell off (S&P -0.71%, Stoxx -0.56%, Asia extending losses) while Fed pricing turns more hawkish (reinforced by Barr) and the ECB's Simkus stays hawkish despite in-line CPI, with RBNZ and RBA also tilting hawkish.
briefs.brief_chain: Renewed US strikes near the Strait of Hormuz lift Brent and EU gas, therefore energy-driven inflation fears push bond yields to multi-year highs, therefore equities fall globally while Fed/ECB pricing turns more hawkish (Barr, Simkus) despite softer US data, and RBNZ/RBA also lean hawkish.

distortions.what: Brief frames Brent's rise as caused by the newly-reported Hormuz-area strikes; source shows the day's Brent move (+4.60% to $94.65 at the close) was already driven by 'the latest strikes at the start of the week' before the specific new US strikes near Hormuz were reported (shortly after that close).
distortions.would_the_trade_change: No — the risk-off, Iran-driven oil/yield thesis is identical either way; only the intra-day sequencing is compressed.

distortions.what: Drops Bessent's comment that the Strait of Hormuz will be 'bypassed' in two years via land pipelines, which the source explicitly frames as a countervailing input the market ignored ('despite... Bessent... saying').
distortions.would_the_trade_change: No — a dropped secondary caveat, not a driver of the day's price action or any forward call.

briefs.source_chain: Iran strikes/response plus rising yields drive a risk-off European sales tape (S&P -71bps, oil/yields higher), therefore GS highlights a short gas-consumers/long power-price-sensitive-utilities pair on the gas spike, flags DELL's beat-and-raise (AI server demand) with a raised EPS estimate and $425 target, stays constructive on European equities on valuation/FCF yield, and upgrades Deutsche Bank to Buy on a 3-year ROTE improvement, alongside notes on BTC ETF flows and the CLARITY Act vote.
briefs.brief_chain: Risk-off tape on Iran headlines and higher yields, therefore GS runs a gas-consumers-short/utilities-long pair, raises DELL's EPS estimate and keeps a $425 Buy target on the AI-server beat-and-raise, stays constructive on Europe, and upgrades Deutsche Bank to Buy on the ROTE story, plus BTC ETF and CLARITY Act notes.

distortions.what: Brief says GS 'keeps Buy' on DELL; source only states the current rating and target ('BUY with $425 px target') without indicating whether this is a reiteration or a new call.
distortions.would_the_trade_change: No — the actionable call (Buy, $425) is identical regardless of whether it is a continuation or new rating.

distortions.what: Drops the €43.75 price target attached to the Deutsche Bank Buy upgrade.
distortions.would_the_trade_change: No — the upgrade call itself (Buy on ROTE improvement) is preserved; only a supporting figure is omitted.

briefs.source_chain: August ISM manufacturing misses and softens across components, while the S&P Global PMI and GS's own survey tracker paint a firmer regional picture, and JOLTS/construction data are mixed with GDP tracking unchanged, therefore Tuesday's tape sees cyclicals lag defensives amid Iran-driven higher yields/oil (with the ISM miss alongside), SPX -71bps, while DELL's beat-and-raise sends shares up after hours and GS's own ETF-short positioning stat shows unusually low shorts.
briefs.brief_chain: ISM manufacturing misses on softer components, so cyclicals lag defensives, while PMI/GS's own tracker show regional strength despite the ISM miss; JOLTS/construction/GDP tracking are mixed but stable; equities close lower on Iran-driven yields/oil (SPX -71bps) while DELL's beat-and-raise pushes shares up after hours; ETF shorts stay near historic lows.

distortions.what: Brief's sentence structure implies the ISM miss caused cyclicals to lag defensives ('...below expectations..., so cyclicals lagged defensives'); source attributes the cyclicals-vs-defensives move primarily to rising yields/oil from the Iran escalation, with the ISM print cited as running 'alongside' that, not as the driver.
distortions.would_the_trade_change: No — both the ISM miss and the cyclicals underperformance are accurately reported; only the causal ordering between two true facts is compressed, and no trade or stance turns on which one is primary.

briefs.source_chain: Falling APAC/US/EU futures on yields and oil, driven by a debated mix of geopolitics, fiscal, AI-issuance crowding-out, inflation and hawkish central-bank repricing, therefore JPM's Market Intelligence desk turns tactically cautious/neutral on global equities and takes profit on gold, but still expects an attractive Q4 given the manufacturing upturn and Asia positioning having fallen from elevated levels with resumed EM inflows, so it keeps a regional preference of long US/Asia vs Europe (with a separate tactically-bullish EU long since May now getting fresh index hedges) built around supercycle longs, plus an EM trade menu, a range-bound USD/JPY call, and a positioning wrap on HF de-grossing.
briefs.brief_chain: Falling futures on yields/oil amid debated bond-selloff drivers, therefore the desk turns tactically cautious/neutral and takes profit on gold, but still expects an attractive Q4 on the manufacturing upturn and improving-but-still-cautious Asia positioning, keeping a long US/Asia vs Europe stance built on supercycle themes with added index hedges, alongside an EM menu, a range-bound USD/JPY call, and an HF de-grossing wrap.

distortions.what: Brief cites Asia positioning falling '75th percentile to the 40th' using the executive-summary figure ('today'), without flagging that the source's own detailed section states a fall to the 32nd percentile over a different stated window (mid-June to late-July) — an inconsistency inside the source itself that the brief silently resolves by picking one number.
distortions.would_the_trade_change: No — both figures support the same qualitative read (positioning down from an elevated level, room to keep buying); the specific percentile doesn't change the medium-term-long call.

distortions.what: Brief merges the relative regional call ('long US/Asia vs Europe') with the note that 'index hedges' are being added, without preserving that the source's incremental hedge ('adding cheap index hedges now') applies specifically to a separate, since-May tactical EU long turning more cautious, not to the supercycle-longs bucket (which the source says is already hedged via momentum options).
distortions.would_the_trade_change: No — the overall portfolio stance (long US/Asia relative to Europe, hedged, still long supercycle themes) is unchanged; only which specific position the newest hedge attaches to is blurred.

briefs.source_chain: Systematic/CTA positioning is already high with vol-control allocations maxed at the 100th percentile, and BofA's model shows systematic strategies would sell in both down and up markets ($163bn down, $9bn even in an up market), therefore there is little incremental buying capacity left even as GS's own conditional projections corroborate a violent down-market unwind, and with McElligott calling the vol collapse 'epic' and warning of possible major losses, plus peak buybacks about to fade into the September blackout window, the flow backdrop is a headwind regardless of market direction.
briefs.brief_chain: Systematic positioning is high and vol-control allocations are maxed out, and BofA shows large selling in a down market versus buying in an up market, therefore GS's conditional projections corroborate limited upside support and a violent downside unwind, and with vol collapse called 'epic' and possible trading losses flagged, plus buybacks fading into the blackout window, flows are becoming a headwind.

distortions.what: Brief states BofA models '$9bn bought in an up market'; the source states BofA models systematic strategies would SELL $9bn even in an up market ('sell $163bn in a down market... and sell $9bn in an up market'). This inverts the sign of the up-market flow estimate.
distortions.would_the_trade_change: Yes — the source's whole thesis is that there is 'not much incremental buying left' because systematics sell in down, flat, AND up scenarios; the brief's reversed figure implies real buying support exists in an up market, which contradicts the note's core no-buying-power warning and would change how a reader weighs upside flow support versus downside unwind risk.

distortions.what: Brief softens McElligott's warning of 'major trading losses may soon surface' to 'warns of possible trading losses,' dropping both the 'major' magnitude and the near-term timing.
distortions.would_the_trade_change: No — the directional warning (vol collapse raises the risk of losses) survives; only its emphasis is diluted.
